AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #15
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 1 hour 30 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water removes heat too quickly
   C. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

2. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Soil Erosion Control? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Soil Erosion Control.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Soil Erosion Control.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Soil Erosion Control.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Soil Erosion Control.

3. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Ice melting to water
   C. Iron rusting
   D. Milk souring

4. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. joule (J)
   C. pascal (Pa)
   D. newton (N)

5. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Urban and peri-urban Agriculture? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Urban and peri-urban Agriculture.

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Animal Health: Disease Control? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Animal Health: Disease Control.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Animal Health: Disease Control.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Animal Health: Disease Control.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Animal Health: Disease Control.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Crop Protection: Disease control? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Crop Protection: Disease control.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Crop Protection: Disease control.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Crop Protection: Disease control.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Crop Protection: Disease control.

8. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Decomposers only

9. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Only carbon dioxide
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Glucose and oxygen

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Livestock Nutrition? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Livestock Nutrition.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Livestock Nutrition.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Livestock Nutrition.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Livestock Nutrition.

11. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Ornamental Cropping? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Ornamental Cropping.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Ornamental Cropping.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Ornamental Cropping.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Ornamental Cropping.

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Forage Crops? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Forage Crops.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Forage Crops.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Forage Crops.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Forage Crops.

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals.

14. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Overgrazing continuously
   B. Removing all vegetation
   C. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   D. Burning crop residue every week

15. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

16. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Powered Agricultural Implements? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Powered Agricultural Implements.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Powered Agricultural Implements.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Powered Agricultural Implements.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Powered Agricultural Implements.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
17. In three clear sentences, explain Non- conventional Livestock and Companion Animals and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

18. In three clear sentences, explain Urban and peri-urban Agriculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

19. In three clear sentences, explain Powered Agricultural Implements and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

20. In three clear sentences, explain Agricultural Biotechnology and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Agri- business Accounts and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Business and Career Opportunities in Agriculture and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
